Emma,

Appreciate the clear list — this is exactly the kind of pragmatic framing we prefer. TL;DR: we can support an "escrow-lite" pattern that limits what we hand over, defines a small set of triggers, and adds witnessing/certification options. I'll let Rachel / Legal confirm precise contract language, but operationally here's what we propose:

- Triggers (narrow): insolvency/bankruptcy of Redwood; material and uncured breach of the MSA affecting the customer's right to run the service; or a mutual termination where both parties agree to full handback. We prefer to avoid open-ended "audit-only" triggers.
- Deliverables: a forensic snapshot of the licensed model binaries & configuration (redacted per agreed PII policy), operator runbook (procedural steps to start/stop/verify service), and a packaged witness certification (PDF signed by Redwood ops lead describing handover steps and checks performed).
- Scope limits: we can exclude telemetry logs by default and provide a clearly scoped subset of metrics needed to validate functionality. Network isolation details can be provided as an exhibit with limited granularity.
- Timeline: standard SLA is 30 business days to prepare a verified snapshot after a valid trigger; can compress to 10 business days for an escalated, paid rush.
- Audit window: we can offer a one-time customer-led witness inspection tied to the handover (2–3 business days on-site or via recorded walk-through). Recurring periodic access requires separate agreement.

Next steps: Rachel, can you propose redline language for the MSA addendum and the order form exhibit? Laura — can you confirm any territory/termination carveouts that affect triggers? Emma — Thurs 09/30 09:30 PT works from our side; sending calendar invite.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

Sean / Laura / Emma —

Quick legal summary and proposed concessions. I attached a tracked redline (Viridian_MSA_v3_redlines.pdf) but call out the principal items here so procurement and security can digest quickly:

1) Trigger language (MSA §12.4 addendum):
   - We propose enumerated triggers only: (a) bankruptcy/insolvency; (b) material breach uncured for 60 days relating to data custodianship or access; (c) expiration/termination where customer has paid for continuity and requests handback.
   - We have pushed back on "audit-only" triggers; instead suggest a named escalation path to an independent technical arbiter if the customer believes Redwood is non-compliant.

2) Evidence scope (Exhibit D — Evidence & Handover):
   - Redwood will provide: (i) a read-only forensic snapshot of deployable artifacts; (ii) operator runbook (procedural, not internal-source-of-truth runbook); (iii) witness certification signed by two Redwood officers.
   - Exclusions: PII, raw telemetry, and internal CI/CD secrets. Where PII may be embedded in artifacts, we'll provide a redacted artifact plus a certified statement describing redaction approach.

3) Timing & costs:
   - Standard timeline 30 business days; expedited 10 business days with a one-time fee (propose to reference order form for rush fees).

4) Audit/witnessing:
   - Offer a one-time witnessed verification (2 business days) included in handback; additional inspections billed under professional services.

5) IP protection & narrow license grant:
   - We will include a limited, revocable license to use the delivered artifacts only for the purpose of running the customer's instance in accordance with the MSA. No right to re-distribute or sublicense.

6) Redlines attached: I limited language that would disclose internal optimization kernels and implementation details; instead we will provide interface-level verification steps and test vectors to confirm functional parity.

Next steps for this thread:
- Sean: confirm operational details above.
- Laura: confirm any termination carveouts for enterprise customers in EMEA (this is US-only for Viridian but flagging).
- Emma / Viridian: review the attached redline and identify any items that are a showstopper. We can move the rest to scope negotiation and tradeoffs.

Regards,
Rachel Kim
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
